precepts.text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.
precepts.point: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
Luke gives the same word Christ spoke in Matthew 12: “And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.” It shall not be forgiven. A word against Christ himself can be forgiven; a word against the Holy Ghost, the power of Christ, what he was doing, cannot.

Why did he say it? Because of what they said earlier in the chapter: he casteth out devils by devils. Christ answered, No, I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, and if I do that, the kingdom is here with you, meaning himself. Christ was healing the people with the Spirit of God, and they said the spirit he was using to heal was the devil. They were speaking evil of his power. That is blaspheming the Holy Spirit itself.

Mark, Peter's scribe, gives the same account in more detail. “He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.” Christ asked them, “How can Satan cast out Satan?” Why would Satan cast himself out? That makes no sense. “And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand”; that is why we fell. “And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.” That is happening right now, America and Israel turning against each other, America burning bridges and going against NATO. Esau has an end.

Then Mark makes it plain: “he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.” Ghost, spirit: same thing, don't let the words fool you. That's the difference. They said the power Christ used to heal the people did not come from God but from the devil, and if they kept that mindset to death, that was it for them.

Brought to now: those who were once enlightened, who “were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, and then fall away and call this truth a cult, blaspheme that same Spirit. Die in that without repenting and you're finished, a dead man or a dead woman walking.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will; thy law is within my heart. God defines his will as his law, which is what the servant in Luke 12:47 knew and did not do.
precepts.point: To whom men have committed much, they will ask the more. If you have skills that can fill offices, more offices will be committed to you. If you cannot be used you are useless. Upper leadership keeps the phone on twenty-four hours a day because there is that much going on across Israel.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Christ says “that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.” What is the will of God? David defines it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

God defines his will as his law. His will for us is that we keep the commandments. So the servant in Luke 12:47 who knew his Lord's will is the one who knew the laws of God and prepared not himself.

Preparing yourself means measuring yourself against the Bible, men and women alike. The Bible is the measuring barometer we look at to see whether we are pairing ourselves off right with God. If we are really honest and examine ourselves, in many cases we are not: if Christ came back right now, many of us are not ready. It comes down to opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing what it says.

Much was given to us. We have the keys to the kingdom of heaven: the will of God, which people live a whole life and never understand, thinking a Hail Mary or gospel songs will have them holding hands with Jesus in the kingdom, not knowing that believing is an action word. Because we know his will, much more will be required of us, and as you move up in rank the road gets narrower until you have to walk blameless. We tell the people to do this and not do that, so we had better live it, or we will be beaten with many stripes.

precepts.text: All things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
precepts.point: A brother deported from France for refusing to stop teaching is now in Ghana and doing well. Papers and citizenship can be taken away, so prepare.

note.label: Civil War & the Son of Perdition

precepts.why:
“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.” Every hair on your head is numbered, so nothing can happen to you unless the Lord allows it. Don't be living and rolling in fear, and don't be scared of no damn ICE. A man's going is of the Lord. The spirit of Christ dwells in you; you are valuable.

Paul adds, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.” If you love God, whatever happens, even bad things in your life, happens for good. When Aquila and Priscilla were deported, it was for good: they ended up as Paul's helpers teaching the gospel. God had a plan for them.

“To them who are the called according to his purpose.” Every last one of us is called according to God's purpose. None of us knows where our going is or what the Lord has planned for us, but he has a purpose for each of us.

A brother in France was told to stop teaching the word of God or leave. He would not stop, so they labelled him an extremist, refused to renew his papers, and deported him. Right now he is in Ghana, doing good, all praises to the Lord. So don't think papers, a green card or citizenship will protect you; laws are being set up to take them away from those who speak against America or Christianity. If they take your green card and send you back, it is what it is, of the Lord. Don't run, don't cry and lose your dignity; make preparation, and go over there and teach the word, because all things work together for good to them that love God.

precepts.text: I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death and destruction.
precepts.point: I am come to send fire on the earth. Suppose ye that I am come to give peace? I tell you, nay, but rather division.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
This is the state of mind of the God we worship. Christ said, “I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?” The fire is already kindled. “Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division.” Christians believe Jesus Christ is about peace in this wicked kingdom. Nah. Christ came to bring division, war and destruction.

Ezra shows what that fire is: “Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” Plagues upon the world: the sword, famine, death, destruction, war and diseases. And who is bringing these things? The Lord. Christ is the one sending these plagues on the earth.

You Christians running around with Jesus is love and everybody love: that is not realistic, and that is not what Christ came to bring. You can pray to white Jesus from now till whenever, but nothing is going to change; it is going to get worse and worse. He went on vacation during slavery and didn't hear you then.

We are living in the beginning of sorrows. If you think it is bad now, you don't understand yet; you are going to see some real horrible things take place on this earth, and shame on those who go back into the world. This year America is 250 years old, the average lifespan of an empire. That is why Trump is so gung-ho about making it great again: it is declining, and what it was built on is unravelling. The fire is kindled, and the plagues are coming.

precepts.text: Be not afraid of them that kill the body; but I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.
precepts.point: Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: the Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life, so make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
Moses says who Israel is dealing with: “the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward”. That is what needs to be taught in the church, who we are really dealing with. Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: “Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

Men can only kill the body. The Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life. That is why the command comes first to “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked”: make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him. Yea, fear him.

precepts.text: Christ said fear not them that kill the body, but fear him which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; five sparrows are sold for two farthings, yet not one is forgotten before God, and the very hairs of your head are numbered. That is how much power the Most High holds.
precepts.point: This shows the power of the Most High over the animals: he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will, just as he did Elijah.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.” Instead, “Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

“Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God? But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.” That is how much power the Most High holds. Not one bird is forgotten before him, and he has command over them all.

So when the word of the Lord sent Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, he could say, “I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.” And “the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening”. The Most High has power over the animals, and he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will. “Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.”

precepts.text: Fear not little flock, it is the Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom; the kingdom is going to that flock, the Israelites.
precepts.point: We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, this Bible. This Bible tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth. That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
We are “the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand”, and Christ speaks to that same flock: “Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.”

Fear not, little flock; it is the Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. The kingdom is going to that flock, the Israelites, the sheep of his hand scattered to the four corners of the earth.

That is why the voice of this Bible needs to reach our people today: to tell the lost sheep who they are, to give them praise and uplift them in their spirits, because the kingdom belongs to the little flock.

precepts.text: Nothing is covered that shall not be revealed, nor hid that shall not be known.
precepts.point: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” The man who hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him; there are seven abominations in his heart. But his cover does not hold: his wickedness is put out on display before the whole congregation.

Christ says why: “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.” Hatred covered by deceit is still covered, and nothing covered stays covered. It will be revealed and known.

Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit. That thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High.

precepts.text: When they bring you before the magistrates and powers, take no thought what to answer, for the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
precepts.point: Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Peter filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean he was shaking, sweating or speaking in tongues. It means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers, exactly as Christ promised: “And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.”

That is how brother Abiel spoke eloquently in court and was released. You must be wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, and the wisdom of God will speak through you in that same hour.

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

precepts.why:
“And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body”. Don’t be afraid, brothers, of no man that could only kill your body. That is what our Lord and our King told us: don’t fear nobody that could just kill you. When it comes to death, it is more than just your body dying. This body is just something to carry you, your spirit. Even when you die and leave this flesh, that’s not the end of it.

“And after that have no more that they can do”: they can’t do nothing else after they kill your body. Man can do that, but other things can be done to you after you leave this physical body, and guess who could hurt you after you leave this body: Christ.

“I will forewarn you”: I’m warning you before time “whom ye shall fear”. “Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell”. Christ is going to be killing people. He kills you, and after he kills your body he takes your spirit and casts it into that Lake of Fire, that torment, and that is going to be set up right here in America.

Christ says, don’t fear him that could just kill you in this body, but fear him that is going to kill you and after he kills you is going to torment you. Even if you’re dead and sleeping: wake up, time for you to feel some pain for all that evil you were doing. You’re going to feel pain after death; that’s what the scripture says in the time of the dead, that they should be judged.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why: Faithful in what? Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.” The faithful steward of Luke 12:42 is faithful in Christ Jesus.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why: The wise steward: “Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.” It is only through God’s commandments that we become wise, wiser than our enemies. This verse carries through the whole beginning of the lesson.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
“The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.” Only the wise in heart are going to receive the Commandments. A prating fool is a fool of lip: somebody that likes to run their mouth and slander.

When you hear brothers or sisters say to hell with the Commandments, you don’t need no Commandments, get the hell away from them. There’s a lot of Israelite camps that echo those very sentiments, and some of you might have run from them and come in here.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
“Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.” The wise man’s heart, his mind, discerns. “Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.”

When you are that wise brother, that wise sister keeping the Commandments, you are considerate of time and judgment. You are well aware when it’s time to go, when it’s time to shut up, when it’s time to move, and when judgment is about to come.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
What does it mean to be made ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season? It’s a reward. Christ says, “Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” The second came saying, “Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds”, and to him likewise: “Be thou also over five cities.”

That is rulership. To the servant who had a little and multiplied it, be ruler over ten cities. A city is big, a city is huge: you need power, you need authority to be over a city. Christ is going to make us rulers over this planet, and that is the portion of meat in due season: the kingdom.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
Ruler over all that he hath: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” Under the whole heaven is the whole planet earth. We’re going to get the world back; we’re going to rule the planet.

“Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom”: the kingdom that’s coming is going to be everlasting. “And all dominions shall serve and obey him”: everybody’s going to be subject to Christ. Everybody on the planet, do or die, and we will be the enforcers.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations.” To overcome is to overcome the sins of this world and your personal sins. To keep the works of Christ is to keep the Commandments, unto the end.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.” We’re going to rule the nations with a rod of iron, with rigor, with austerity; we ain’t playing with nary one of them. We’re going to break the nations like a potter breaks a vessel. To break the nations we need power: some of you got a 9 millimeter, but you got 15 shots and a hundred out front. That ain’t going to work. Christ is going to give us that power.

“Even as I received of my Father”: the same blessings Christ got, he is going to give to us. Your church never taught you that, because your pastor don’t know the Bible.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
“And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.” That’s why Christ said in Revelation 2, “even as I received of my Father”: because we’re joint heirs with him. Joint heirs means what Christ gets, we get.

“If so be that we suffer with him”: we got to go through some stuff. It’s always going to be hard times; tribulation is coming, persecution is coming, and we have to endure it. That is when you’re going to be that real joint heir and get that power, “that we may be also glorified together.”

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
Christ speaking: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” Those that say, I ain’t following no black Jesus, no black Yahawashi, the hell with that.

That’s why we’re going to be his enforcers on this earth. You read these parables and it’s all in there, but the church goes, I don’t know what that means.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why: His portion with the unbelievers: “Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more.” Who are the sinners? That’s Israelites. And the wicked is the white man. Let both be no more: it’s the same judgment. “Bless thou the Lord, O my soul. Praise ye the Lord.”

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
“But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth”: the wicked is Esau. “And the transgressors shall be rooted out of it”: the transgressors are you and me, if we decide to break the Commandments; you online in those funky donkey camps.

There it is again: the same judgment. The Israelite who breaks the Commandments gets his portion with the unbelievers.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why: Neither did according to his will. So what’s his will? “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” God’s law is his will, and God’s will is his law. Never be confused about the will of God: the servant who did not do according to his will is the one who did not keep the law.

note.label: Identifying Babylon The Great

precepts.why:
Beaten with many stripes: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name?” Lord, we was on the streets teaching Yahawah, Bahasham, Yahawashi; and they were also cursing people out, slandering and lying on people. “And in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?”

“And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” Christ is going to say I never knew you, to you evil brothers out there and your simple followers, the few you got. To work iniquity is to break the Commandments.
